digest.en: North Korea announced a test of submarine‑launched cruise missiles off its east coast, marking the latest addition to its expanding arsenal.
digest.hi: Iran's deputy chief of staff warned that any vessel attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz will face immediate military response. Simultaneously, Russia accused Kyiv of rejecting peace talks following recent strikes on its oil refineries.

articles.title: Small states must have say as world shapes new compact with tech giants: Vivian Balakrishnan
articles.summary: Singapore's foreign minister Vivian Balakrishnan urged small states to secure a voice in a new global compact with tech giants. He called for shared norms and guardrails to accelerate technology adoption while managing associated risks. The proposal seeks to balance innovation speed with broader international stability. Dr Balakrishnan called for a compact between governments, tech firms and the wider international community to "develop common norms and guardrails so that we can accelerate the pace of technology and reap its benefits, but also deal with the risks".

articles.title: Zelenskyy Vows Refinery Strikes, Expresses Anger At US Intel Disruption
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the resumption of attacks on Russian energy facilities. He also expressed anger over a dangerous disruption of US satellite intelligence that hindered Ukrainian operations. Ukrainian forces have struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, Russian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would resume attacks on Russian energy facilities and voiced anger over a "dangerous" disruption of satellite intelligence from the United States.

articles.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
articles.summary: Global tech markets suffered a deep sell-off driven by inflation fears and AI sector debt. Shares in Samsung and SoftBank plunged as traders worried about potential interest rate hikes. The decline reflects growing anxiety over the heavy borrowing underpinning current artificial intelligence infrastructure. Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook marketsBusiness news – live updatesLarry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through.

articles.title: North Korea says it tested cruise missiles designed to be fired from submarines
articles.summary: North Korea announced submarine-launched cruise missile tests. State media cited readiness assessments. The tests aimed to improve naval strategic capabilities. Officials highlighted the reliability of the nuclear deterrent. North Korean state media said the tests were aimed at assessing the readiness of the country's underwater combat systems, improving the Navy's ability to carry out strategic missions and demonstrating the reliability of its nuclear deterrent.

articles.title: Houthi attack on Saudi oil giant raises global energy concerns
articles.summary: Iran-backed Houthis targeted the headquarters of Saudi oil giant Aramco in Dhahran. The strike damaged parts of the facility but caused no fatalities. The attack highlights the rebels' growing ability to hit strategic targets deep inside Saudi Arabia. The conflict in Yemen has entered a dangerous new phase after Iran-backed Houthi rebels targeted the headquarters of Saudi oil giant Aramco in Dhahran.

articles.title: US banks on bunker-busting Tomahawks to crack China’s missile wall
articles.summary: The US Navy plans to award Raytheon a sole-source contract for bunker-busting Tomahawk missiles. The move aims to counter deeply buried missile sites protected by robust air defenses. However, the system faces significant logistical and escalation challenges if deployed against China. The US Navy’s bunker-busting Tomahawk push reflects growing recognition from the Iran war that striking deeply buried missile sites protected by robust air defenses requires long-range standoff weapons.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
articles.summary: Senegal authorities detained more than 320 LGBTQ+ individuals since February after the government tightened its law criminalising homosexuality. The arrests triggered forced HIV testing and limited access to legal representation, according to a Human Rights Watch report. The crackdown signals a broader clamp At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reportsMass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report. More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, accor.

articles.title: Oil prices retreat as investors weigh supply outlook, West Asia tensions
articles.summary: Brent crude dropped 1.6 percent to 104.42 dollars a barrel. West Texas Intermediate fell one percent to 94.11 dollars. Investors reassessed global supply risks. The retreat reversed previous session gains. Brent crude futures fell $1.64, or 1.6%, to $104.42 a barrel by 0337 GMT, while U. S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 98 cents, or 1%, to $94.11, reversing gains from the ‌previous session.

articles.title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region
articles.summary: Indonesia is testing dry ice dispersal in South Sumatra. The government deployed planes to combat toxic haze. This follows failed cloud seeding attempts. Regional neighbors remain angry over the smoke. Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South SumatraAs fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice. Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fire.

articles.title: Ukrainian gain on a drone-filled battlefield
articles.summary: Ukraine announced Operation Vivaldi in mid-September. Forces retaken territory near Lyman. The offensive disrupted Russian advances. Gains remain limited despite heavy drone activity. Russia’s drone and missile attacks on Ukraine’s population and infrastructure continue to dominate coverage of the conflict. But on the ground, Ukraine has been making significant, if still limited, gains. In mid-September, Ukraine formally announced the existence of Operation Vivaldi, which has retaken territory near Lyman and disrupted a Russian advance toward the fortified cities [] The post O.

articles.title: Girls In Hijabs Turned Away From Azerbaijani Schools Amid Protests Over Dress Code
articles.summary: Azerbaijani parents and students protested after schools barred girls wearing hijabs from classes. The dispute followed a new ban on clothing deemed incompatible with secular education. The move has intensified friction between religious families and state policy. A new dress-code dispute in Azerbaijan’s public schools has sparked protests by parents and students after reports that girls wearing hijabs, or Islamic headscarf, were turned away from classes.

articles.title: Ukraine Tests AI-Powered Drones As Debate Grows Over Autonomous Weapons
articles.summary: Ukraine is deploying artificial intelligence in drones to track and engage targets. Military officials confirm humans retain control over lethal decisions. Developers caution that fully autonomous weapons systems are approaching operational reality on the battlefield. Ukraine is increasingly using artificial intelligence in drones and other battlefield systems to track, identify, and attack targets. Military officials say humans still remain in control of lethal decisions, but developers warn that fully autonomous weapons are moving closer to reality.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau's health minister stated the government did not authorize a Danish-led hepatitis B trial in newborns. The study, backed by the US government and private partners, would not test vaccine safety or effectiveness. The ministry denied approval for the controversial research. Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK JrGuinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday. The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would inst.

articles.title: EU Working On Multiple Fronts To Limit Russians From Entering Bloc
articles.summary: The European Union is developing measures to restrict Russian citizens from entering the bloc. Officials are considering a total ban on non-essential travel into the Schengen zone. These efforts aim to limit movement across multiple policy fronts. The European Union is working on multiple fronts to limit the number of Russian citizens that can enter the bloc, including the nuclear option of a total ban on all non-essential travel into the club’s Schengen zone.

articles.title: Gaza braces for winter amid attacks, joint patrols in CAR, 90 cities commit to sustainable
articles.summary: The UN and partners are preparing for winter in Gaza despite ongoing attacks on civilians. OCHA highlighted the urgent need for cold and rainy season support. Humanitarian efforts continue amid persistent violence and displacement in the territory. The UN and its partners are stepping up preparations in Gaza for the approaching cold and rainy season, even as attacks affecting civilians continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
articles.summary: The WHO reported over 125,000 suspected cholera cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The epidemic has caused 3,644 suspected deaths since January 2025. This surge occurs while the country simultaneously battles an ongoing Ebola outbreak. The cholera epidemic continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 suspected deaths were recorded between January 2025 and the end of September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Wednesday.

articles.title: WFP warns of potential ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ as fighting blocks aid delivery
articles.summary: The UN World Food Programme warned of a humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen. Intensifying fighting has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people. Blocked roads and shifting frontlines severely restrict access to Taiz and other conflict zones. Intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people as shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restrict access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Survivors Rescued From Kyiv Building After Deadly Russian Strike
articles.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv overnight, killing three people and injuring over twenty others. Survivors were rescued from a damaged building. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Western partners provided no advance warning of the attack, highlighting a gap in intelligence sharing. Moscow launched a wave of ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv overnight, killing at least three people and injuring more than 20.

articles.title: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign
articles.summary: Russia continues its aerial campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure, targeting apartment buildings, bridges, and power plants. As winter approaches, Kyiv residents are preparing for potential outages. The sustained attacks on the electricity grid aim to degrade civilian resilience during the colder months. Russia shows no sign of letting up on its escalating aerial campaign against Ukraine’s apartment buildings, bridges, power plants, electricity grid, and other targets.

articles.title: US Navy’s SSN(X) won’t arrive for years as China closes sub gap
articles.summary: The US Navy issued a sources-sought notice for its next-generation SSN(X) attack submarine. This move addresses the aging fleet while China closes the undersea gap. Chinese shipyards now offer superior capacity and acoustic stealth, challenging American naval dominance in the region. As the US Navy lays the groundwork for its next-generation SSN(X) attack submarine to replace its aging fleet, the US’s longstanding undersea supremacy faces an intensifying test against China’s rapid naval buildup, advancing acoustic stealth and superior shipyard capacity.

articles.title: 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China
articles.summary: Satellite imagery confirms the Taliban completed a road to the China-Afghanistan border. Beijing shows no signs of opening the militarized boundary. The infrastructure project remains a dead end for trade routes. Satellite imagery sourced by RFE/RL confirms Taliban claims they have completed a road that leads up to China's remote border with Afghanistan. However there is no indication Beijing intends to open the militarized boundary any time soon.

articles.title: How Ukraine's Strikes On Data Centers Disrupted Taxis, Shopping, And Business In Russia And Beyond
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones hit three Yandex data centers. Repairs will take months. The strikes disrupted taxi services, online shopping, and business operations across Russia and other countries where the tech firm operates. Ukrainian drone strikes on three data centers operated by Russia’s Yandex will reportedly take months to repair and have caused widespread disruption in everyday life across Russia and other countries the sprawling tech company operates in.

articles.title: 800 million young people face a future without jobs
articles.summary: The UNDP head warned 800 million young people in developing economies will lack jobs. This projection covers the coming years without immediate action. The agency launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment. 800 million young people face a future without jobs.

articles.title: ‘Need for UN has never been greater,’ UN chief says, proposing slimmer $3.3 billion budget for 2027
articles.summary: António Guterres proposed a $3.3 billion budget for 2027. This represents a $40.8 million cut from previous plans. He cited climate disruption, AI, war, and hunger as drivers for the need. Amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger, “the need for the United Nations has never been greater,” Secretary-General António Guterres said on Tuesday, presenting a $3.3 billion programme budget proposal for next year – a cut of $40.8 million.

articles.title: Germany Starts Nord Stream 'War Crime' Trial With Prosecutors Blaming Ukrainian 'State Authorities'
articles.summary: German prosecutors will begin a war crime trial regarding the Nord Stream pipeline explosions. The case marks the first public, sworn testimony on the incident after years of speculation. Prosecutors are blaming Ukrainian state actors for the sabotage. After four years of speculation, leaks, and briefings by anonymous sources, the world is finally about to hear evidence given publicly under oath in a German courtroom about how the Nord Stream gas pipelines were blown up -- in a case that could prove politically explosive.

articles.summary: ईरान ने अमेरिका को चेतावनी दी है कि होर्मुज स्ट्रेट पर उसका नियंत्रण बना रहेगा। अमेरिका दावा करता है कि उसकी नेवी जलमार्ग पर पूर्ण नियंत्रण रखती है। ईरान ने रणनीतिक जलमार्ग को बंद कर दिया है। दोनों देश आमने-सामने हैं। अमेरिका का कहना है कि उसकी नेवी का इस रणनीतिक जलमार्ग पर पूरा कंट्रोल है और सामान की सामान्य शिपिंग व्यवस्था भी फिर से शुरू कर दी गई है, तो वहीँ ईरान का कहना है कि होर्मुज स्ट्रेट पर हमेशा से ईरान का ही कंट्रोल रहा है और आगे भी ऐसा ही रहेगा।

hi.title: ‘अमेरिकी सेना के अभियानों की जानकारी लीक करने वालों की गोली मारकर कर देनी चाहिए हत्या’ – डोनाल्ड
hi.summary: ट्रंप ने बुलहेड सिटी में रैली के दौरान सेना की जानकारी लीक करने वालों को मारने की बात कही। यह टिप्पणी मिडटर्म चुनावों से पहले की गई। अमेरिका (United States of America) में मिडटर्म चुनाव से पहले राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप (Donald Trump) अलग-अलग जगह रैलियाँ कर रहे हैं। एरिज़ोना की बुलहेड सिटी में एक रैली के दौरान अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति का आक्रामक अंदाज़ दिखा और उन्होंने अमेरिकी सेना के अभियानों की जानकारी मीडिया में लीक करने वालों के प्रति अपनी नाराज़गी जताई।

articles.title: लद्दाख के नेताओं और MHA के बीच निर्वाचित निकाय पर आज बातचीत, विशेष मॉडल पर बनेगी सहमति!
articles.summary: लेह में लद्दाख के नेताओं और गृह मंत्रालय के अधिकारियों के बीच उप-समिति स्तर की बैठक होगी। चर्चा अनुच्छेद 371(K) के तहत विशेष संवैधानिक सुरक्षा उपायों के रोडमैप पर होगी। केंद्र शासित प्रदेश स्तर पर निर्वाचित निकाय के प्रस्ताव पर भी बातचीत होगी। LAB और KDA के नेता इस बैठक में शामिल होंगे। अनुच्छेद 371(K) के तहत लद्दाख के लिए विशेष संवैधानिक सुरक्षा उपायों के रोडमैप और केंद्र शासित प्रदेश स्तर पर एक निर्वाचित निकाय के प्रस्ताव पर चर्चा करने के लिए, आज लेह में लद्दाख के नेताओं और गृह मंत्रालय (MHA) के अधिकारियों के बीच उप-समिति स्तर की बातचीत का एक नया दौर शुरू होगा.

articles.title: जापान सागर में पहुंची किम जोंग की पनडुब्बी, लगातार दागी दो मिसाइलें, हिले दक्षिण कोरिया-अमेरिका
articles.summary: उत्तर कोरिया ने जापान सागर में पनडुब्बी से दो रणनीतिक क्रूज मिसाइलों का परीक्षण किया। KCNA ने कहा कि इसका मकसद समुद्री लड़ाकू प्रणालियों की तैयारी परखना था। यह परीक्षण दक्षिण कोरिया के साथ बढ़ते तनाव के बीच हुआ है। दोनों देश हाल में मिसाइल और हाइपरसोनिक हथियारों के परीक्षण कर चुके हैं। North Korea News: उत्तर कोरिया ने बुधवार को पूर्वी सागर, जिसे जापान सागर भी कहा जाता है, में पनडुब्बी से लॉन्च होने वाली दो तरह की रणनीतिक क्रूज मिसाइलों का परीक्षण किया.

articles.summary: पीएम मोदी ने लद्दाख में 3,350 करोड़ रुपये की पांच विकास परियोजनाओं का उद्घाटन किया। इन परियोजनाओं से सड़क और हवाई संपर्क बेहतर होगा। बिजली की सुविधाओं को मजबूती मिलेगी। सांस्कृतिक विरासत का संरक्षण होगा और पानी की उपलब्धता बढ़ेगी। प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने गुरुवार को वीडियो कॉन्फ्रेंसिंग के माध्यम से लद्दाख में करीब 3,350 करोड़ रुपये की पांच प्रमुख विकास परियोजनाओं का उद्घाटन और लोकार्पण किया.

articles.title: इमरान खान को 'लीव इंडिया' नोटिस, क्या पुलिस के पास था अधिकार? जानिए OCI कार्ड के नियम
articles.summary: मुंबई पुलिस ने अभिनेता इमरान खान को 28 अक्टूबर तक भारत छोड़ने का नोटिस दिया। यह निर्देश उनके ओसीआई कार्ड और विदेशी नागरिकता से जुड़े नियमों के आधार पर है। मामला उनके एक विरोध प्रदर्शन में शामिल होने से जुड़ा है। बॉलीवुड अभिनेता आमिर खान के भांजे और अभिनेता इमरान खान को मुंबई पुलिस द्वारा 'भारत छोड़ने का नोटिस' दिए जाने के बाद से कानूनी और राजनीतिक गलियारों में हलचल तेज हो गई है.
